habitat: Vleis, dams, grassland and cultivations when breeding. Otherwise it wanders widely in flocks, often with other weavers.
summary: A common resident. The breeding male has a yellow crown, nape and back, black underparts, a black bill and pink legs. He displays with puffed plumage and whirring wings, making buzzing sounds. The female and non-breeding male are small and compact, with a dark mantle and a whitish belly. The Kemp paper name Golden Bishop and the code VB were left unchanged.

similar.note: Southern Red Bishop is red and black in breeding plumage. Yellow-crowned Bishop has a yellow crown and black underparts.

calls.description: The breeding male makes various buzzing sounds while displaying with puffed plumage and rapidly whirring wings. Grade A call from Arrozal Nossa Senhora do Rosário, Faro, Portugal. No southern African grade A recording outranked it. The filename is XC829310-230908-171338Arcebispo.mp3.

research.note: Newman calls it a common resident, and Avibase does not mark it rare, so all twelve months are listed. It is nomadic outside the breeding season. The Kemp code VB was left unchanged. The only Kruger photograph is a distant breeding male. No non-breeding photograph and no flight photograph were found. The grade A call is from Portugal. Population figures and the Kemp name Golden Bishop were left unchanged.
